Introduction

A reader's letter in The Guardian's Brief letters page on 22 November 2026 offers a simple answer to the urge to skip tracks: play one album all the way through. The letter, from Bren Pointer of London, responds to Adrian Chiles's column of 18 November 2026, 'Instant gratification is ruining our lives – and for me it started with my CD player's shuffle button'. In it, Chiles traces his own concentration challenges back to the shuffle button on his first CD player.

The suggestion

Pointer's solution is specific: play Aja by Steely Dan, 'in its glorious 39 minutes and 54 seconds' entirety', with 'absolutely no skipping or shuffling of tracks'. The letter presents it as a promise: play the album in full and there will be no skipping or shuffling.

The column behind the letter

In his column, Chiles writes that he first met the shuffle button on his first CD player in 1989. Back then he would listen to whole albums such as Edie Brickell and New Bohemians' Shooting Rubber Bands at the Stars and Bob Dylan's Blood on the Tracks. He contrasts that with today, when he catches himself scrolling on his phone while watching television. He also cites a 2020 study that found one in four songs is skipped within five seconds, with only about half of songs heard in full. He notes that Spotify's 2025 Wrapped counts an album as listened to once a listener reaches 70% of its tracks. He also writes that he asked listeners of his radio programme who still listens to full albums, and wonders whether the harder question is who actually finishes a single song. He warns that skipping music, words, pictures and films could lead to what he calls 'species oblivion'.

The rest of the page

The letters page also carried a reply about hot toddies. William Bryce of Farnham, Surrey, suggested flavouring the hot water with sugar and lemon, then swishing the teeth with 'a generous helping of whisky'. It was a reply to a dental hygienist's concern about hot toddies raised in a letter on 20 November. The page's listed topics were Steely Dan, hot toddy, dental advice, Christmas gifts and Black Friday.
